title: The new song of baptism: horse and rider drowned, the baptized clothed with heaven
english: Let us sing the new song, for behold, Adam has been made new and Eve has been carried up to the heavens, and the devil has been thrown into the fire. Let us borrow that song from Miriam, the sister of Moses, for it suits us now just as it suited them then. Let the chorus of those saints stand with us and sing what they sang aloud then at the Red Sea: “Let us sing to the Lord, for he is gloriously glorified” (Exodus 15:1). What has he done? “Horse and rider he has thrown into the sea” (Exodus 15:10). Horse and rider: the horse is lust-mad sin, and the rider is the demon seated upon sin, and in the baptismal washing he sank them both. Let us sing then to the Lord, for he is gloriously glorified, for “Pharaoh and his power he has thrown into the sea” (Exodus 15:4)—that is, the devil and his dark and defiled army of demons he drowned in the washing of baptism. I no longer fear to hear, “Earth you are, and to earth you shall return” (Genesis 3:19), for in baptism I put off the earth and put on heaven, and I hear: Heaven you are, and to the heavens you shall return. For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ, and: As is the man of dust, so are those who are of dust; and as is the man of heaven, so are those who are of heaven (1 Corinthians 15:48). We must mount upon the clouds and run up to the heavens. The word is not without witness; hear Paul saying: “We shall be caught up in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air, and so we shall always be with the Lord” (1 Thessalonians 4:17). Therefore, as we have just heard the psalmist urging us and saying, “This is the day the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it” (Psalm 118:24 (117:24 LXX)), let us rejoice then, not darkened by drunkenness and dissipation—for that would not be gladness but folly and darkening of heart. Let us rejoice, leaping in the Spirit; let us rejoice, feasting on love, rejoicing in hope. And if we must also consider another gladness of heart, let us receive the heavenly bread with pure hands and send it on to the soul as provision for eternal life. With pure hands, I say—not washed with ordinary water, but made bright by good deeds. And let us draw the divine and heavenly mixture with rose-colored lips, reddening them not with any crimson dye but making them purple with the blood of Jesus Christ. O truly great and good day, on which the lamb is slain and the world is purchased and our shepherd lives! For he says, “I am the good shepherd” (John 10:11). O new mystery and strange wonder! The cross stood and Christ was stretched out, and what appeared was an unjust death, but what was happening was a holy bridal chamber; what appeared was a cross, but what was being accomplished was a bridal chamber. Yesterday the bridal chamber was set up, and today a people was born. O death of Christ, death of death, pouring forth sweet life in the bitterest death! O mystery of Abraham being accomplished in Christ!
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Amphilochius is preaching to the newly baptized, urging them to take up the song of Miriam at the Red Sea as the type of their own baptismal victory.

title: The Cross as the World's Sail and the Many Names of Christ
english: Isaac was being bound by the feet on the altar, and a lamb was being slaughtered in his place; and the Son of God was being carried up on the cross and was being crucified in the flesh for us, and while the flesh was suffering, the divinity was not suffering. The sail of the cross stood in the ship of the world, and the world remained unshipwrecked; the one who sails with this sail of the cross knows no shipwreck of death, but sails up into the heavens. Eve no longer fears the reproach of Adam, for in Mary her fault has been saved; Adam no longer fears the serpent, for Christ crushed the head of the dragon. For you, he says, crushed the head of the dragon upon the water, that is, upon baptism. I no longer mourn, I no longer weep saying: I was turned to misery when a thorn was stuck in me; for Christ came, uprooted the thorn of our sins, and placed it on his own head. My ancient grief is loosed, the old curse is loosed that says: Thorns and thistles the earth shall bring forth for you; for the thorns are dried up, the thistle is uprooted, and a triple-woven crown has been placed on my head. Who among Jews and Greeks believes that wood stood and life blossomed? And every day it is harvested by the faithful, and the fruit remains unspent; and every tribe and every nation of the faithful climbs this tree with the step of the soul and fills the bosom of the mind with immortal fruit, and the tree carries all and feeds all and seals all and enriches all, and after these things hurls them into the heavens. For what did Christ not endure on our account, that he should be called Christ? We cannot count his names, but I attempt to speak, beloved: door, way, sheep, shepherd, worm, stone, pearl, flower, angel, man, God, light, spring, sun of righteousness. The many-named Christ is also one; the many-named Son is also one, not turning, not changing, for the divinity is unchanging; but fitting himself to each matter according to the working, he has set a proper name for each working. And let us see, beloved, if we can present the working for each name. He was called way: For I am, he says, the way and the truth, because he himself became the leader of all the virtues and of the ascent into the heavens. The same one is door: For I am the door of the sheep, because through him, as through a door, we enter into the kingdom of the heavens. He was called salt, because he wiped away the stench of idolatry from human beings and seasoned our souls with faith for the return to piety and bound together the loosened limbs of the mind with truth.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Amphilochius is preaching to the congregation about the newly baptized, and has just described the cross as a bridal chamber; now he moves from the type of Isaac to the cross as the world's sail and begins listing the many names of Christ.

title: The many names of Christ and their works, closed with a doxology
english: He was called sheep: For he was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb silent before its shearer (Isaiah 53:7). He was called sheep because of the slaughter, and because of the partaking of his holy members, and because of the immortal protection that comes from the seal of his holy blood. He was called shepherd: For I am the good shepherd (John 10:11), because he turned back the sheep that had gone astray and killed the lion who opposes us with the staff of the cross. He was called pearl because, like a pearl in an oyster between two folds, he was born from a virgin without the seed of a man, or because he is the adornment of the soul, or because of his many-shining, pure radiance flashing everywhere with the brightness of divinity. He was called light—for he was the true light, which enlightens every person coming into the world (John 1:9), because he drove the dark error of the old gloom from our minds and opened the eyes of our ruling intellect, so that we might truly see that the things we once worshiped are not gods but works of human hands, stones and wood. He was called cornerstone because, having built the two peoples like two walls by faith, he rests upon them, gathering them into one bond of salvation. He was called sun of righteousness because of his brightness and warmth—for there is nothing hidden from his heat—and because of the twelve-rayed light of the apostles. He was called mustard seed because he makes himself small and comes down to our capacities at the beginnings of faith; then, when he has nestled into the furrows of our soul and spread into its depths, it rises to a heaven-high height and is kindled toward piety and wisdom. He was called worm: For I am a worm and not a man, because he hid his flashing divinity like a hook in the worm of his body, let himself down into this deep of life, and like a good fisherman drew up his catch, fulfilling what was written: You will draw the dragon with a hook. He was called man because he wore a body not composed from pleasure and sleep, but having come to be from a virgin and the Holy Spirit. But since each of us, beloved, receives also the honey-flowing teaching of the fathers, let us seal here the purse of our words with the Holy Spirit, so that when they come from the honey-dripping wisdom of our Lord Jesus Christ they may fill the cisterns of our hearts, and each of you may sprout much fruit of piety—one producing thirty, another sixty, another a hundred, the crown of the angels—in Christ Jesus our Lord, with whom to the Father be glory, honor, and might, together with the holy and life-giving Spirit, now and to all the ages of ages. Amen.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Amphilochius is finishing his list of Christ's names, explaining each name by a work of Christ, and then he closes the homily by deferring to the fathers' teaching and blessing the congregation.
